critique: The three orange pulse-wave rings sit on top of the white mark ring at scale 100 and fade up to 90% opacity over the first 4–6s. This tints the ring salmon for most of the piece, then it snaps to white as each wave leaves, so the mark's own color is unstable. The waves also expand with Cubic In, so they accelerate away and are almost invisible (5.83s) instead of reading as a sharp hit on 5s and 6s.

Keep each wave at 0 opacity until its beat, then fire it on that beat: snap to about 80% at scale 100, expand to about 200 with a fast Expo/Cubic Out over roughly 0.5s, and fade with it. This keeps the ring a clean, consistent white and turns the post-drop beats into visible, punchy secondary hits.
